name: portclash
displayName: PortClash: Find Port Conflicts Across Compose, .env & Dev Servers
description: Finds "port already in use" before you run anything: collects every declared port in docker compose, .env, package.json scripts, Vite/Next.js/Angular/Astro dev servers, devcontainer, launch.json and Kubernetes, and flags clashes, databases exposed on 0.0.0.0 and macOS AirPlay ports.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: PortClash only reads workspace files. The optional live port check (portClash.checkListening, off by default) can only be switched on from user settings while a workspace is untrusted.

portClash.enabled.description: Scan the workspace for declared ports and report conflicts.

portClash.checkListening.markdownDescription: Also check whether declared ports are already in use on this machine (PC005). Linux: reads `/proc/net/tcp` and `/proc/net/tcp6` (no sockets). macOS/Windows (ports 1024 and above only): opens and immediately closes a local connection to `127.0.0.1:<port>` (no data is sent); if that is refused, briefly listens on `127.0.0.1:<port>` with Node's `net` module and closes it again. Never contacts any other host. Ignored from workspace settings while the workspace is untrusted.

portClash.ignorePorts.description: Ports to ignore entirely (not listed, never reported).

portClash.databasePorts.description: Container ports treated as databases/caches for PC003 (published on all interfaces).

enumDescriptions: Always flag 5000/7000 (teammates on macOS hit it even if you do not).
Only when VS Code runs on macOS.
portClash.airPlayNote.description: When to report ports 5000 and 7000 (used by AirPlay on macOS) as PC002.

portClash.privilegedPortNote.description: Report non-Docker dev servers that bind a privileged port below 1024 (PC002).

portClash.codeFallbacks.description: Check PORT env var fallbacks in JS/TS/Python code against .env and compose (PC004).

portClash.exclude.description: Glob patterns (relative to the workspace folder) that are never scanned.

portClash.maxFiles.description: Maximum number of candidate files read per scan.
